youtube.title: Why Are Stop Signs Octagons? (And Why They Used to Be Yellow)
youtube.description:
Why is a stop sign an octagon, the only one on American roads? In 1923 highway officials gave every road sign shape a meaning: the more sides, the bigger the danger. The stop sign history also explains why it's red and why it used to be yellow.

From Detroit's first white square stop sign in 1915 to the circle saved for railroad crossings, why you can read a stop sign from behind or under snow, and why stop signs were yellow until 1954: this is the hidden why behind the stop sign.

Chapters
{CHAPTERS}

Sources
- Federal Highway Administration: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) history - https://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/kno-history.htm
- Smithsonian Magazine / Detroit Historical Society: the first stop sign (Detroit, 1915)
- MUTCD 1954 edition: stop signs changed to red with white letters
